lessons.title: The Kisumu Tray: Eight Substances, Many Puzzles

quiz.prompt: Before any test, Otieno writes in his notebook: "Sulphur (D) will float on water because it looks light." What is this statement at this point in the lesson?
choices: An observation of sulphur floating on water
A scientific explanation of why sulphur floats
A prediction with a reason, which still has to be tested
A result that proves how sulphur behaves in water
quiz.rationale: The learners have not put anything in water yet, so the statement is a prediction with a reason. Predictions are recorded before evidence and tested later.
quiz.placement: Predict: individual prediction and group prediction table (Substance, Prediction, Reason)

quiz.prompt: Learners are at a tray with eight substances in a school laboratory in Kisumu. Which is the correct way to observe them?
choices: Smell each container closely to tell the substances apart
Skip the goggles because most of the substances are ordinary things from home
Wear goggles and use only your eyes and a hand lens
Taste a tiny amount of the white grains to be sure they are salt
quiz.rationale: In the observation activity learners wear goggles, do not taste, and do not sniff from the container. They use their eyes and the hand lens only.
quiz.placement: Observe: recording substances A-H in the observation table

quiz.prompt: Learners record what substance E, iron filings, looks like on the Kisumu tray. Which description fits what they would record?
choices: A clear liquid
A yellow powder
A white tablet
Grey and gritty grains
quiz.rationale: In the observation table, E (iron filings) is described as grey and gritty. Sulphur is the yellow powder and the tablets are white.
quiz.placement: Observe: observation table for substances A-H

quiz.prompt: One group sorts the eight substances into "powders" and "not powders". A second group sorts the same eight into "things I use in food" and "other things". Salt appears in a group in both sorts. What does this show?
choices: One of the groups must have made a mistake, because a substance can only belong in one group
Substances can be sorted only by colour
The same substance can belong to different groups, depending on the rule used to sort
Only the teacher can decide which group a substance belongs in
quiz.rationale: Each group chose its own rule and then a second rule. The same substances can be grouped in many ways by the visible characteristics chosen. There is no single "right" grouping yet.
quiz.placement: Observe: two different sorts using sorting cards A-H

quiz.prompt: Salt (A), sugar (H) and sand (C) all look like small grains. After sorting and comparing them, what can the class say at this point in the lesson?
choices: Because they look alike, all three will behave in the same way
Looking alike does not tell us how they will behave, so tests are needed
Looking is enough to know exactly what a substance will do
Because they look alike, all three will vanish in water
quiz.rationale: The class has only looked, sorted and predicted. Appearance alone cannot show how a substance behaves, so they need tests (planned for Lesson 2).
quiz.placement: Explain: 'Is it enough to look at a substance to know what it will do?' discussion

quiz.prompt: Wanjiru asks: "The antacid tablet and the paracetamol tablet both look like white tablets, so why does one help heartburn and the other help pain?" At this point in the lesson, what is the best response?
choices: It is because one tablet is whiter than the other
It is because one tablet is bigger than the other
It has not been explained yet, so we write it as a question on the Driving Question Board
It is because both are white tablets, so they do the same job
quiz.rationale: Lesson 1 is for noticing and wondering, and no explanation is given. Wanjiru's puzzle is recorded on a sticky note for the Driving Question Board and followed up in later lessons.
quiz.placement: Driving Question Board: posting and clustering questions, including Wanjiru's question

quiz.prompt: A group fills in a "What I notice / What puzzles me" T-chart about the Kisumu tray. Which entry belongs under "What I notice"?
choices: Why is too much medicine dangerous?
F and G are both white tablets
Can salt be taken out of water?
Why might sulphur burn?
quiz.rationale: An observation is something learners can see on the tray, such as both tablets being white. The other three entries are questions about things not yet known or tested.
quiz.placement: Explain: 'What I notice / What puzzles me' T-chart

lessons.title: Matter: Mixing, Separating and Heating the Kisumu Tray

quiz.prompt: A learner stirs 2 g of table salt into 50 mL of water and the salt vanishes, leaving a clear liquid. Which statement is correct?
choices: The salt has dissolved and can be recovered by evaporating the water
The salt has been destroyed, so it cannot be got back
The salt has melted because the water is warm
The salt has sunk to the bottom where it cannot be seen
quiz.rationale: Dissolving does not destroy a substance. The salt is mixed through the water and evaporation brings it back (2.7 g was recovered from mixture M).
quiz.placement: Part A: water test (salt A and sugar H dissolve)

quiz.prompt: A learner adds 1 level spatula of sand, and another adds 1 level spatula of sulphur powder, to separate beakers of water at about 25 C and stirs gently. Which result is correct?
choices: Sand sinks and stays visible, while sulphur floats and is not wetted
Both sand and sulphur dissolve to give clear solutions
Sand dissolves and sulphur sinks
Sand floats and sulphur dissolves
quiz.rationale: Neither substance dissolves. Sand sinks and stays visible, while sulphur floats on top and refuses to wet. Powders that look alike do not behave alike.
quiz.placement: Part A: water test (sand C and sulphur D)

quiz.prompt: A salt solution is poured through filter paper into a clean beaker. What passes through the filter paper into the beaker?
choices: Only the water, because the salt is caught on the paper
Both the water and the dissolved salt
Nothing passes through because the paper blocks the solution
Only the salt, because the water stays behind
quiz.rationale: Dissolved salt particles are mixed among the water particles and are too small to be caught by filter paper. This is why salt needs evaporation, not filtration.
quiz.placement: Part B: mixture M separation (trying to filter a salt solution)

quiz.prompt: Mixture M is a dry mixture of iron filings, sand and salt. Which order of steps separates all three substances?
choices: Use a magnet to remove the iron, add water and filter out the sand, then evaporate the filtrate to recover the salt
Add water and filter, then use a magnet on the filtrate, then evaporate the sand
Filter the dry mixture, then use a magnet on the salt, then add water to the sand
Evaporate the dry mixture, then use a magnet, then filter
quiz.rationale: Iron is magnetic, so it is removed first from the dry mixture. Sand does not dissolve, so it is filtered out of the water, and the dissolved salt is recovered by evaporating the filtrate.
quiz.placement: Part B: mixture M separation (magnet, filtration, evaporation)

quiz.prompt: A group started with 9 g of mixture M. They recovered 2.9 g of iron filings, 2.8 g of dry sand and 2.7 g of salt. How many grams were lost during the separation?
quiz.rationale: Total recovered = 2.9 + 2.8 + 2.7 = 8.4 g. Loss = 9 - 8.4 = 0.6 g, which can be explained by spillage or material sticking to the equipment.
quiz.placement: Part B: mixture M separation (mass table 9 g in, 8.4 g out)

quiz.prompt: Which property correctly separates sulphur from sand when each is heated in a dry test tube?
choices: Sulphur dissolves in water but sand does not
Sulphur is attracted by a magnet but sand is not
Sulphur melts at about 115 C and burns with a blue flame, while sand shows no change
Sulphur does not change on heating, but sand melts and burns
quiz.rationale: Sulphur melts to a runny liquid and then burns with a blue flame and a choking smell. Sand does not change. Sulphur does not dissolve and is not magnetic.
quiz.placement: Part C: heat test (teacher demonstration)

quiz.prompt: Solid sulphur is heated until it melts at about 115 C. Which statement best describes what happens to its particles?
choices: The particles stop moving and stay in fixed positions
The particles disappear and new particles are made
The particles gain energy and move more, staying close together as a liquid
The particles move apart until they fill the whole test tube like a gas
quiz.rationale: In a solid the particles are tightly packed. With heat they move more and the solid becomes a liquid, where the particles are still close together but able to move around.
quiz.placement: Second step: particle pictures of solid, liquid and gas (melting of sulphur, paracetamol and sugar)

quiz.prompt: The class smells the sharp, choking sulphur dioxide gas from across the laboratory. Which particle idea best explains this?
choices: Gas particles are close together and slide slowly over each other
Gas particles are heavier than air, so they must sink to the floor and stay there
Gas particles are far apart and move independently, so they spread to fill the space
Gas particles are tightly packed in a fixed shape, so they stay near the flame
quiz.rationale: Gas particles are far apart and move independently, so a gas spreads out to fill the whole container or room. Solids and liquids do not spread like this.
quiz.placement: Second step: particle pictures (smell of sulphur dioxide spreading as a gas)

quiz.prompt: Which of the following is a CHEMICAL property of a substance?
choices: Iron filings being attracted by a magnet
Sulphur burning with a blue flame
Sugar melting at about 186 C
Salt dissolving in water
quiz.rationale: Burning and reacting with acid are chemical properties. Magnetism, melting point and solubility are physical properties.
quiz.placement: Third step: CER paragraph (physical versus chemical properties)

quiz.prompt: An antacid tablet fizzes when dropped into vinegar, but a paracetamol tablet does not. What does this evidence show?
choices: Paracetamol has been destroyed by the vinegar
Both tablets must dissolve in the same way because they look alike
The two tablets are the same substance because both are white tablets
The antacid reacts with acid but paracetamol does not, so they are different substances with different properties
quiz.rationale: Fizzing with acid is a chemical property of the antacid, and paracetamol shows no reaction. Substances that look alike can have different properties because of what they are made of.
quiz.placement: Third step: using properties to answer Wanjiru's puzzle about the antacid (F) and paracetamol (G)

lessons.title: Matter Continued: Classifying Substances and Building Class Model v1

quiz.prompt: A learner says: 'The antacid tablet and the paracetamol tablet are both white powders, so each one must be a single pure substance.' Which response is best?
choices: Correct, because every tablet is made of only one element.
Wrong, because tablets cannot contain any compounds at all.
Looking the same does not show a substance is pure; we need evidence from tests such as dissolving, heating and reacting.
Correct, because anything that looks like a powder is one substance.
quiz.rationale: Appearance alone cannot tell us whether a substance is one thing or several. Evidence from properties and separations is needed, so 'white powder means pure' is a misconception.
quiz.placement: Predict: silent prediction and sticky-note chart of 'pure single substance' vs 'mixed' (antacid F and paracetamol G)

quiz.prompt: A group separates a mixture of 3 g iron filings, 3 g sand and 3 g salt (total 9 g). They recover 2.9 g of iron, 2.8 g of sand and 2.7 g of salt. How much mass was lost?
quiz.rationale: Recovered mass = 2.9 + 2.8 + 2.7 = 8.4 g. Loss = 9 - 8.4 = 0.6 g, caused by spillage and material sticking to equipment.
quiz.placement: Task 2: re-trace the separation of mixture M and calculate 2.9 + 2.8 + 2.7 = 8.4 g and the loss

quiz.prompt: Salt has dissolved completely in water. Why can the salt NOT be removed from the water by filtration or by a magnet?
choices: The filter paper reacts with salt and destroys it.
The salt has turned into water and no longer exists.
The dissolved salt is mixed in the water and passes through the filter paper; it is not magnetic, so it must be recovered by evaporation.
The salt is magnetic but too heavy to filter.
quiz.rationale: Dissolved salt passes through filter paper together with the water and is not attracted by a magnet. Evaporating the water leaves the salt behind.
quiz.placement: Task 3: salt dissolved in water passes through the filter paper and needs evaporation

quiz.prompt: In a mixture of iron filings, sand and salt, the iron is still pulled by a magnet, the sand is still gritty and does not dissolve, and the salt still dissolves in water. What does this show?
choices: The mixture is a single element.
The substances have lost their properties.
The three substances have joined to form one new compound.
The substances are only mixed, so each keeps its own properties and can be separated by physical methods.
quiz.rationale: In a mixture, substances are not chemically joined, so each keeps its own properties. This is why magnetic separation, filtration and evaporation work.
quiz.placement: Task 3: each part of mixture M kept its own properties, so M is a mixture

quiz.prompt: Iron (Fe) is classed as an element, but salt (sodium chloride) is classed as a compound. Which reason is correct?
choices: Iron is a solid, but salt dissolves in water.
Iron is made of only one kind of substance (iron), while salt has two different elements, sodium and chlorine, joined together.
Salt is a mixture of sodium and chlorine that can be separated with a magnet.
Iron is a compound of iron and sulphur.
quiz.rationale: An element is one kind of substance that cannot be split into simpler ones by ordinary methods. A compound has different elements joined together; salt is sodium and chlorine joined.
quiz.placement: Classification card sort: Element, Compound or Mixture (iron E, salt A) with the Substance Information Card

quiz.prompt: An antacid tablet contains calcium carbonate, which is a compound, together with binders. Why is the whole tablet classified as a mixture?
choices: Because tablets are always made of exactly one element.
Because calcium carbonate is an element.
Because it fizzes in vinegar.
Because it contains an active ingredient and binders that are only mixed together, not joined into one substance.
quiz.rationale: A mixture has different substances just mixed together. The tablet has the active ingredient plus binders, so it is a mixture even though one part is a compound.
quiz.placement: Card sort discussion: 'Why is the antacid tablet F a mixture even though it contains a compound, calcium carbonate?'

quiz.prompt: In a test, an antacid tablet fizzes in dilute vinegar, but a paracetamol tablet shows no fizz. Which conclusion is best supported by this evidence?
choices: Paracetamol is an element and the antacid is a mixture of iron and sulphur.
Both tablets work in the same way because both are white.
The antacid reacts with and neutralises acid, while paracetamol has a different active ingredient that works on pain and fever instead.
Paracetamol is stronger than the antacid because it does not fizz.
quiz.rationale: The fizz shows that the antacid reacts with acid, which explains why it relieves heartburn. Paracetamol does not react this way; it works on pain and fever by a different action.
quiz.placement: Wanjiru's puzzle: why the antacid relieves heartburn while paracetamol relieves pain (fizz-in-vinegar evidence)

quiz.prompt: An adult paracetamol label says: take 1 to 2 tablets of 500 mg every 4 to 6 hours, with a maximum of 8 tablets in 24 hours. What is the maximum total mass of paracetamol in 24 hours, in grams?
choices: 4 g
8 g
quiz.rationale: 8 tablets x 500 mg = 4000 mg. Since 1000 mg = 1 g, the maximum is 4 g in 24 hours. Taking more can damage the liver.
quiz.placement: Medicine safety: paracetamol label dose and the 4 g per 24 hours maximum with the liver warning

lessons.title: Meaning of Chemistry as a Field of Science: Defining Chemistry from the Tray Evidence

quiz.prompt: After comparing their drafts, a class in Kisumu agrees on one definition of Chemistry using evidence from their tray of substances. Which definition did they agree on?
choices: Chemistry is the science that studies living things and how they grow.
Chemistry is the science that studies only dangerous liquids used in laboratories.
Chemistry is the science that studies matter: its composition, properties, changes and uses.
Chemistry is the science that studies forces, motion and energy.
quiz.rationale: All four columns of the evidence chart (composition, properties, changes, uses) describe matter, so Chemistry is the science that studies matter and these four aspects. The other options describe a misconception or other sciences.
quiz.placement: Explain: groups draft and the class agrees one class definition of Chemistry

quiz.prompt: A group fills in a four-column evidence chart with the headings Composition, Properties, Changes and Uses. Which entry belongs in the Changes column?
choices: Sulphur burns with a blue flame and gives a sharp, choking-smelling gas.
Sand sinks in water and stays visible.
Iron filings are pulled out of a mixture by a magnet.
Paracetamol tablets are used to relieve pain and fever.
quiz.rationale: Burning sulphur forms a new substance (sulphur dioxide), so it is a change. Magnetism and sinking are properties, and relieving pain is a use.
quiz.placement: Observe: four-column evidence chart (Composition, Properties, Changes, Uses)

quiz.prompt: In the tray investigation, mixture M of iron filings, sand and salt had a mass of 9 g. After separating it with a magnet, filtration and evaporation, the learners recovered 2.9 g of iron, 2.8 g of sand and 2.7 g of salt. What mass was lost during the separation?
quiz.rationale: Mass recovered = 2.9 + 2.8 + 2.7 = 8.4 g. Mass lost = 9 - 8.4 = 0.6 g.
quiz.placement: Observe: mixture M data (9 g in, 8.4 g recovered)

quiz.prompt: Learners test the definition 'Chemistry is the science that studies matter: its composition, properties, changes and uses' on this question: why does table salt dissolve in water but sand does not? Which answer uses the definition correctly?
choices: Sand is not matter, so it cannot dissolve.
Both dissolve if stirred long enough, so the difference is only in the stirring.
Salt and sand are different substances with different properties (such as solubility) that come from what each is made of.
Sand is heavier than salt, and all light solids dissolve in water.
quiz.rationale: Each substance has its own properties, such as solubility, which come from its composition. Sand is matter, and in the tray test it did not dissolve however it was mixed.
quiz.placement: Explain: challenge case (a) why salt dissolves but sand does not

quiz.prompt: Wanjiru asks why an antacid tablet relieves heartburn while a paracetamol tablet relieves pain. The antacid fizzes in dilute vinegar, but paracetamol does not. Which explanation is correct?
choices: The antacid reacts with and neutralises excess stomach acid, while paracetamol relieves pain and fever by a different action and does not neutralise acid.
Both tablets neutralise acid, but paracetamol does it more slowly.
Paracetamol relieves heartburn by reacting with stomach acid, and the antacid relieves pain by melting in the body.
The antacid is matter but paracetamol is not, so they act differently.
quiz.rationale: Fizzing in vinegar shows the antacid reacts with acid, which is why it relieves heartburn. Paracetamol does not fizz and does not neutralise acid; it relieves pain and fever in a different way.
quiz.placement: Explain: challenge case (c) Wanjiru's question about antacid F and paracetamol G

quiz.prompt: A paracetamol label says an adult may take a maximum of 8 tablets of 500 mg each in 24 hours. What is this maximum in grams? (1 g = 1000 mg)
choices: 4 g
quiz.rationale: 8 tablets x 500 mg = 4000 mg. Dividing by 1000 gives 4 g. Taking more can damage the liver.
quiz.placement: Explain: why taking too much of either medicine is dangerous (paracetamol maximum 4 g in 24 hours)

quiz.prompt: A learner says, 'Chemistry only studies dangerous liquids in a laboratory.' Which is the best reply based on the class definition of Chemistry?
choices: She is wrong, because Chemistry only studies medicines.
Chemistry studies all matter, including ugali, tea from Kericho and the water in Lake Victoria.
She is right, because Chemistry cannot study solids such as sand or sugar.
She is right, because chemists only work with dangerous liquids.
quiz.rationale: Chemistry studies the composition, properties, changes and uses of all matter, not only dangerous liquids or laboratory work, and not only medicines.
quiz.placement: Model Building: exit ticket on the class definition of Chemistry and tray evidence

lessons.title: Branches of Chemistry: Matching the Five Branches to the Kisumu Tray

quiz.prompt: A class tests two substances. Sugar melts at about 186 C, turns brown and then chars black with a caramel smell. Paracetamol melts at about 169 C and browns. Both are made of carbon-containing substances. Which branch of chemistry mainly studies carbon-based substances such as these?
choices: Inorganic chemistry
Organic means farming without chemicals, so none of the branches
Organic chemistry
Analytical chemistry
quiz.rationale: Organic chemistry studies carbon-based substances such as sugar and many medicines. Here 'organic' does not mean farming without chemicals.
quiz.placement: Card 1: H sugar and G paracetamol

quiz.prompt: Table salt dissolves completely in water. Iron filings are pulled out by a magnet and turn dull blackish when heated. Salts, metals and minerals like these belong to which branch of chemistry?
choices: Biochemistry
Physical chemistry
Inorganic chemistry
Organic chemistry
quiz.rationale: Inorganic chemistry studies substances such as salts, metals and minerals, so salt and iron filings fit here.
quiz.placement: Card 2: A salt and E iron filings

quiz.prompt: Sulphur melts at about 115 C, paracetamol at about 169 C and sugar at about 186 C. Comparing how matter behaves when heated, such as melting points, is mainly the work of which branch?
choices: Analytical chemistry
Organic chemistry
Physical chemistry
Biochemistry
quiz.rationale: Physical chemistry studies how matter behaves, including melting points and energy changes. Analytical chemistry is about finding out what is present and separating or measuring it.
quiz.placement: Card 3: Melting points

quiz.prompt: A mixture M has 3 g of iron, 3 g of sand and 3 g of salt (9 g in total). A magnet recovers 2.9 g, filtration recovers 2.8 g and evaporation recovers 2.7 g. This separating and measuring is analytical chemistry. How much mass was lost during the separation?
quiz.rationale: Total recovered = 2.9 + 2.8 + 2.7 = 8.4 g. Loss = 9 - 8.4 = 0.6 g.
quiz.placement: Card 4: Mixture M separation (magnet, filtration, evaporation)

quiz.prompt: An antacid tablet neutralises excess stomach acid and fizzes in dilute vinegar. Paracetamol relieves pain and fever but does not neutralise acid. Which branch of chemistry mainly explains how each of them acts in the body?
choices: Analytical chemistry
Biochemistry
Physical chemistry
Inorganic chemistry
quiz.rationale: Biochemistry is the chemistry of living things, including how medicines act in the body.
quiz.placement: Puzzle: Wanjiru's question on why the antacid relieves heartburn but paracetamol relieves pain

quiz.prompt: A learner says, 'Paracetamol can belong to only one branch of chemistry.' Which response is correct?
choices: Correct, because paracetamol is a medicine, so only biochemistry studies it.
Wrong, because paracetamol is studied by organic chemistry for what it is made of and by biochemistry for how it acts in the body.
Wrong, because paracetamol is studied only by physical chemistry for its melting point.
Correct, because each substance is studied by only one branch.
quiz.rationale: One substance can belong to more than one branch. Organic chemistry studies the makeup of paracetamol and biochemistry studies its action in the body.
quiz.placement: Explain: Can one substance belong to two branches?

quiz.prompt: A Nairobi company wants to check that every paracetamol tablet it makes contains 500 mg of paracetamol. Which branch of chemistry would investigate this question?
choices: Inorganic chemistry, because tablets are salts
Physical chemistry, because tablets melt when heated
Biochemistry, because paracetamol acts in the body
Analytical chemistry, because it finds out what is present and measures how much
quiz.rationale: Checking how much of a substance is in a tablet means finding out what is present and measuring it, which is analytical chemistry.
quiz.placement: Driving Question Board: groups write a new question a chemist in a specific branch could investigate

lessons.title: Importance of Chemistry in Kenya: From the Kisumu Tray to Our Industries (Model v2)

quiz.prompt: Paracetamol relieves pain and fever, yet taking too much of it is dangerous. Which statement best explains why the same medicine can be both useful and harmful?
choices: Medicines that work faster are always safer, so a bigger dose gives quicker relief with no harm
Only medicines made in factories are harmful, because natural substances are always safe
The amount taken matters: the right dose helps, but more than the safe limit can damage the liver
If a medicine is useful for one illness, it cannot harm any part of the body
quiz.rationale: The lesson stresses that a useful chemical becomes dangerous when the safe amount is exceeded; above 4 g of paracetamol in 24 hours the liver can be damaged. More medicine does not mean faster relief, and 'natural' does not mean safe.
quiz.placement: Predict card: 'Why might the same chemical be both useful and dangerous?'

quiz.prompt: An adult paracetamol label says: take 1 to 2 tablets of 500 mg every 4 to 6 hours, with a maximum of 8 tablets in 24 hours. What is the maximum total amount of paracetamol, in grams, that an adult may take in 24 hours?
choices: 4 g
quiz.rationale: 8 tablets x 500 mg = 4000 mg. Since 1000 mg = 1 g, 4000 mg = 4 g.
quiz.placement: Station 2 - Medicine facts card: calculating 8 x 500 mg = 4000 mg = 4 g

quiz.prompt: The safe adult maximum of paracetamol is 4000 mg in 24 hours. A learner takes 10 tablets of 500 mg each in one day. By how many mg does this go over the safe limit?
choices: 500 mg
quiz.rationale: 10 x 500 = 5000 mg taken. The limit is 4000 mg, so 5000 - 4000 = 1000 mg over the limit, which can damage the liver.
quiz.placement: Station 2 - teacher question: 'If a learner takes 10 tablets of 500 mg in one day...'

quiz.prompt: A teacher puts an antacid tablet in dilute vinegar and it fizzes. A paracetamol tablet in dilute vinegar does not fizz. What is the best conclusion from this evidence?
choices: Paracetamol is stronger than the antacid because it does not fizz
The antacid relieves pain and fever, while paracetamol relieves heartburn
Both tablets do the same job because both are tablets
The antacid reacts with acid, so it can neutralise excess stomach acid, while paracetamol does not neutralise acid
quiz.rationale: Fizzing with vinegar (an acid) shows the antacid reacts with acid, which is why it relieves heartburn. Paracetamol gave no reaction and relieves pain and fever by a different action.
quiz.placement: Station 2 - re-observing F fizzing in dilute vinegar and G giving no fizz

quiz.prompt: In a teacher-led demonstration, a very small amount of sulphur is heated. It melts and burns with a blue flame and a sharp, choking smell. Why is the demonstration done at a safe distance, with goggles, by an open window?
choices: Sulphur is a magnetic substance that can jump towards the learners
The sharp smell shows that the sulphur has dissolved in the air
Sulphur burning makes sulphur dioxide, a sharp choking gas, so burning it needs care
The blue flame shows the sulphur has turned into sand, which is dangerous
quiz.rationale: Burning sulphur forms sulphur dioxide, which has a sharp choking smell and is harmful to breathe. Industries that use burning reactions must therefore handle them carefully.
quiz.placement: Station 3 - teacher-led sulphur (D) demonstration

quiz.prompt: Sugar dissolves completely in water. A sugar factory such as Mumias or Nzoia wants to get solid sugar from a sugar-and-water solution. Which statement is correct?
choices: Dissolved sugar cannot be filtered out, so the water must be evaporated to leave the sugar behind
A magnet will pull the sugar out, as it does with iron filings
Adding more water will make the sugar solid again
Filtering will work, because sugar is a solid like sand
quiz.rationale: Dissolved particles pass through filter paper, so filtering cannot separate sugar from the solution. Evaporating the water leaves the sugar behind. Sand, which does not dissolve, can be filtered.
quiz.placement: Whole-class debrief: 'Salt A and sugar H both dissolve. How does that help a food or sugar factory such as Mumias or Nzoia?'

quiz.prompt: Learners are adding an 'Industries and uses' layer to their class model, with arrows from a property to an industry that uses it. Which arrow is correct?
choices: Burns with a blue flame and a sharp smell, so sulphur is safe to sniff directly
Dissolves in water, so salt and sugar can be removed from water by a magnet
Pulled by a magnet, so sugar is used to make paracetamol
Reacts with acid, so the antacid is used in medicine to relieve heartburn
quiz.rationale: The antacid reacts with and neutralises excess stomach acid, so the property 'reacts with acid' links to the medicine industry. The other arrows join a property to a wrong use or an unsafe action.
quiz.placement: Building model v2: 'Industries and uses' layer with arrows from properties to industries

lessons.title: Careers in Chemistry: Who Works with the Kisumu Tray Substances, and Who Gets to Choose?

quiz.prompt: A pharmaceutical scientist at a Kisumu company tests whether an antacid tablet can relieve heartburn. Which property of the tablet is the scientist mainly testing?
choices: The colour of flame it gives when burnt
How it reacts with acid
Whether it floats on water
Whether a magnet attracts it
quiz.rationale: An antacid works by neutralising excess stomach acid, so the key property is its reaction with acid. Magnetism, floating and flame colour do not explain heartburn relief.
quiz.placement: Predict: learners list three jobs that use the properties of F antacid, G paracetamol or the separation of mixture M

quiz.prompt: A laboratory technician has a mixture of salt, sand and iron filings in water. She pulls out the iron filings with a magnet and then filters out the sand. What should she do next to get the dissolved salt back from the filtrate?
choices: Add more water and stir
Filter the filtrate a second time
Evaporate the water from the filtrate
Use the magnet again on the filtrate
quiz.rationale: Salt is dissolved, so it passes through the filter paper. Evaporating the water leaves the salt behind as a solid.
quiz.placement: Observe: research on analytical chemist or laboratory technician (separating mixture M: magnet, filtration, evaporation)

quiz.prompt: An analytical chemist separates 9 g of mixture M. She recovers 2.9 g, 2.8 g and 2.7 g of the three solids, and 0.6 g is lost during the separation. What is the total mass recovered?
quiz.rationale: Total recovered = 2.9 + 2.8 + 2.7 = 8.4 g. This agrees with 9 g - 0.6 g lost = 8.4 g.
quiz.placement: Observe: research on analytical chemist or laboratory technician (2.9 g, 2.8 g and 2.7 g recovered and 0.6 g lost out of 9 g)

quiz.prompt: Wanjiru asked why an antacid relieves heartburn but paracetamol relieves pain. Which statement gives the correct claim a pharmacist could make?
choices: Antacid neutralises excess stomach acid, while paracetamol relieves pain and fever and does not neutralise acid
Both tablets relieve heartburn because both neutralise stomach acid
Paracetamol relieves heartburn better because it is stronger
Antacid relieves pain and fever, while paracetamol neutralises stomach acid
quiz.rationale: An antacid reacts with and neutralises excess stomach acid. Paracetamol relieves pain and fever but does not neutralise acid, so the two tablets do different jobs.
quiz.placement: Explain: claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph on how pharmaceutical and analytical careers explain why F relieves heartburn and G relieves pain

quiz.prompt: An adult may take a maximum of 8 paracetamol tablets of 500 mg each in 24 hours. What is this maximum in grams? (1 g = 1000 mg)
choices: 4 g
quiz.rationale: 8 x 500 mg = 4000 mg. Dividing by 1000 gives 4 g. Taking more than this can damage the liver.
quiz.placement: Explain: claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph using MEDICINE FACTS (8 tablets of 500 mg = 4 g in 24 hours)

quiz.prompt: Which of these best describes a gender stereotype?
choices: A fact about which careers men and women are trained for
A scientific law that explains why some people are better at chemistry
A fixed idea about what girls or boys can or should do
A rule that only one gender may work in a laboratory
quiz.rationale: A gender stereotype is a fixed idea about what girls or boys can or should do. It is an opinion and not a scientific fact or a rule.
quiz.placement: Explain: stereotype discussion 'What is a gender stereotype?'

quiz.prompt: Otieno says, 'Chemistry jobs like pharmacist or analytical chemist are only for boys.' Which reply is best?
choices: He is right, because most chemists in the past were men
He is wrong only for pharmacists, but right for analytical chemists
A stereotype can limit career choice, but it does not change who can do chemistry; girls and boys can both work in these careers
He is right, because girls are not good at separating mixtures
quiz.rationale: A stereotype is a fixed idea that may discourage some learners, but it does not decide who can do chemistry. The career profiles showed women and men working as chemists, so the claim has no evidence behind it.
quiz.placement: End of lesson: stereotype discussion and plenary presentations on who can do these careers

lessons.title: Consumer Protection and Product Labels: Reading the Story a Label Tells

quiz.prompt: A customer at Otieno's kiosk asks whether a packet of old biscuits is still fine to eat. Which item on the packet label would best tell the customer if the biscuits may no longer be safe?
choices: The picture of biscuits on the front
The weight of the packet
The expiry date
The name of the factory
quiz.rationale: The expiry date shows when a product may no longer be safe or effective, which is what the customer needs to know. The other items do not tell how long the biscuits stay safe.
quiz.placement: Predict: Otieno's kiosk scenario and group chart 'Must be on a label' / 'Why it matters'

quiz.prompt: A learner inspecting a juice carton finds the KEBS Diamond Mark printed on it. What does this mark tell the buyer?
choices: The juice is cheaper than other brands
The juice contains no preservatives
The juice will never go bad
The product has met quality standards set by the Kenya Bureau of Standards
quiz.rationale: The KEBS Diamond Mark shows that a product has met quality standards. It does not mean the product lasts forever, and it says nothing about price or about preservatives.
quiz.placement: Observe: label kit inspection, column 'KEBS Diamond Mark?'

quiz.prompt: Learners compare the label on a maize flour packet with the label on a paracetamol 500 mg box. Which information would they expect to find on the paracetamol box but NOT on the maize flour packet?
choices: A list of ingredients
The dose and a warning that too much can damage the liver
An expiry date
The name of the manufacturer
quiz.rationale: Food labels list ingredients, preservatives and nutritional information. Medicine labels carry the active ingredient, dose and cautions. Both types can have an expiry date and a manufacturer name.
quiz.placement: Observe: comparing food labels (maize flour, juice) with medicine labels in the label observation table

quiz.prompt: The paracetamol label says: 'Adult dose: 1 to 2 tablets of 500 mg every 4 to 6 hours. Maximum 8 tablets in 24 hours.' What is the greatest total mass of paracetamol an adult may take in 24 hours, in grams?
choices: 4 g
8 g
quiz.rationale: 8 tablets x 500 mg = 4000 mg. Since 1000 mg = 1 g, this is 4 g in 24 hours.
quiz.placement: Explain: calculating the daily maximum for paracetamol (8 x 500 mg = 4000 mg = 4 g)

quiz.prompt: A customer wants to give a small child 2 tablets of paracetamol 500 mg, because 2 tablets is within the adult dose. Why is this unsafe?
choices: A child's dose is worked out from body weight and is much smaller, so an adult dose can overload a child's liver
Paracetamol only works for adults, so it does nothing in a child
The tablets will not dissolve in a child's stomach
Two tablets is always too few to have any effect
quiz.rationale: A child's dose depends on body weight and is much smaller than an adult dose. An adult dose can overload the child's liver, so the buyer should ask a health worker or pharmacist.
quiz.placement: Explain: answering Otieno's kiosk question about giving a small child 2 tablets

quiz.prompt: A shopkeeper mixes up an antacid tablet and a paracetamol tablet because both look like plain white tablets. Why is this a problem?
choices: Paracetamol neutralises stomach acid and the antacid relieves pain
Only the antacid can be harmful if taken in excess
The two tablets do the same job, so the mix-up only wastes money
Antacid neutralises excess stomach acid for heartburn, while paracetamol relieves pain and fever, so the wrong tablet will not treat the problem and too much of either can harm the body
quiz.rationale: The two tablets have different jobs and different cautions, which is why each needs its own label. An antacid taken too often upsets the body's salts, and too much paracetamol can damage the liver.
quiz.placement: Explain: why antacid F and paracetamol G need different labels

quiz.prompt: Learners add 'Labels and consumer protection' to their class model. On the paracetamol label, what does the warning 'maximum 8 tablets in 24 hours' connect?
choices: The colour of the tablet to its price
The taste of the tablet to the way it is made
The factory's address to the expiry date
The property of the substance in the body (too much can damage the liver) to a safe amount for the consumer
quiz.rationale: The model links a property of the substance (excess damages the liver) to label information (the maximum dose) and then to safe use by the consumer.
quiz.placement: Model Building: adding the layer 'Labels and consumer protection' to class model v2

lessons.title: Drugs and Substance Abuse: Why the Dose Makes the Difference

quiz.prompt: Wanjiru has a bad headache. She says, "If the label says 2 paracetamol tablets, I will take 8 at once so the pain goes away faster." What is the best response?
choices: Paracetamol cannot harm the body, because it is a medicine.
Taking far more than the label says can damage the liver, so she should follow the label.
She is right, because more tablets always mean faster relief.
Eight tablets is safe if she drinks a lot of water.
quiz.rationale: More is not always better. Paracetamol taken above the label dose can damage the liver, so the label dose must be followed.
quiz.placement: Predict: individual and group predictions on what happens if a person takes far more tablets than the label says

quiz.prompt: A teacher drops an antacid tablet F into dilute vinegar (an acid) and it fizzes. Paracetamol tablet G in dilute vinegar does not fizz. What does this evidence suggest?
choices: G neutralises stomach acid better than F.
Fizzing shows that F is poisonous and G is safe.
F reacts with acid, so it can neutralise excess stomach acid, while G does not react with acid.
F and G are the same substance because both are white tablets.
quiz.rationale: F fizzes with acid, so it reacts with acid and can neutralise excess stomach acid. G does not react, so it does not work by neutralising acid. It relieves pain by a different action.
quiz.placement: Part A: teacher demo of F and G in dilute vinegar

quiz.prompt: A paracetamol label says: "500 mg per tablet. Maximum 8 tablets in 24 hours." What is the maximum mass of paracetamol an adult may take in 24 hours, in grams? (1000 mg = 1 g)
choices: 4 g
quiz.rationale: 8 x 500 mg = 4000 mg. Since 1000 mg = 1 g, 4000 mg = 4 g.
quiz.placement: Part B: data card and calculation of the maximum daily mass of paracetamol

quiz.prompt: A paracetamol tablet contains 500 mg. The label maximum is 8 tablets (4000 mg) in 24 hours. A person takes 2 tablets every 4 hours for the whole 24 hours. By how many mg does this go over the label maximum?
quiz.rationale: There are 24 ÷ 4 = 6 doses, so 6 x 2 = 12 tablets, which is 12 x 500 = 6000 mg. The excess is 6000 - 4000 = 2000 mg.
quiz.placement: Part B: calculation of tablets taken at 2 tablets every 4 hours in 24 hours

quiz.prompt: A person takes antacid tablets all day after every meal for several weeks. What is the most likely effect of this antacid overuse?
choices: Liver damage, as with too much paracetamol
No effect, because antacids are always harmless
Upset body salts, with constipation or diarrhoea
Faster relief from pain and fever
quiz.rationale: Antacid taken too often can upset the body's salts and cause constipation or diarrhoea. Liver damage is the effect of paracetamol overdose.
quiz.placement: Building the group explanation on why too much of either tablet is dangerous (data card facts on antacid and paracetamol)

quiz.prompt: A learner takes 10 paracetamol tablets of 500 mg in one day because a headache is severe. The label maximum is 8 tablets in 24 hours. Which statement is correct?
choices: This is following a prescription, because paracetamol is a medicine.
This is correct use, because the learner is only taking tablets and not alcohol.
This is substance abuse, because the amount is harmful and above the label maximum.
This is correct use, because a severe headache needs more medicine.
quiz.rationale: Substance abuse means using a substance in a harmful way or amount. 10 tablets is 5000 mg, which is more than the 4000 mg maximum and can damage the liver.
quiz.placement: Sorting the six Kenyan scenario cards into correct use or misuse (key terms: drug, prescription, dosage, substance abuse)

quiz.prompt: Which statement about alcohol, miraa (khat), bhang (cannabis) and tobacco for school-age learners is correct?
choices: A small amount is a safe dose for a learner.
They only affect the body, not learning or safety.
They are safe if a friend gives them to you.
They are not medicines for learners, and there is no safe dose for a learner.
quiz.rationale: These substances are not medicines for learners. They can harm the body and mind, learning, safety, family and community, and there is no safe dose for a learner.
quiz.placement: Effects of substance abuse: fact cards on alcohol, miraa, bhang and tobacco

quiz.prompt: A group adds a safe-use section to the class model about medicines like antacid F and paracetamol G. Which statement should it include?
choices: Properties decide what a medicine does, and the dose decides whether it helps or harms.
The more tablets a person takes, the faster the medicine works.
Tablets that look the same work in the same way, so the dose does not matter.
A medicine is safe at any dose if it is bought from a shop.
quiz.rationale: The model links properties to how a medicine works, and dose to safety. Labels, prescriptions and correct dosage keep people safe.
quiz.placement: Part A: model revision, adding a section on safe use to class model v2

lessons.title: Safe and Healthy Learning Environment and the Final Model: How Properties of Substances Shape the Products and Medicines We Use

quiz.prompt: Mixture M had 3 g of iron filings, 3 g of sand and 3 g of salt (9 g in all). A group separated it and recovered 2.9 g of iron, 2.8 g of sand and 2.7 g of salt. How much mass was lost during the separation?
quiz.rationale: Total recovered = 2.9 + 2.8 + 2.7 = 8.4 g, so the loss = 9 - 8.4 = 0.6 g. The loss is from spillage and from material sticking to equipment.
quiz.placement: Part A: evidence review, re-checking mixture M (recovered masses and loss calculation)

quiz.prompt: A mixture contains iron filings, sand and salt. Which property of iron lets us remove it from the mixture first, before using water?
choices: Iron is attracted by a magnet
Iron dissolves in water
Iron melts easily when heated
Iron fizzes in vinegar
quiz.rationale: Iron is magnetic, so a magnet pulls it out of the dry mixture. Sand and salt are not attracted by a magnet.
quiz.placement: Part A: evidence review (which property lets you separate the iron from mixture M)

quiz.prompt: Iron has been removed from a mixture of sand and salt. Water is added and the mixture is stirred and filtered. Sand stays on the filter paper and salt passes through with the water. Why?
choices: Salt is magnetic but sand is not
Both sand and salt dissolve, but sand is heavier
Sand dissolves in water but salt does not
Salt dissolves in water but sand does not dissolve
quiz.rationale: Salt dissolves in water, so it passes through the filter paper as a solution. Sand does not dissolve, so it is trapped on the paper. Salt is then recovered by evaporation.
quiz.placement: Part A: evidence review (which property tells you the salt is still in the water)

quiz.prompt: The label on a paracetamol packet says the maximum dose for an adult is 8 tablets of 500 mg in 24 hours. What is this maximum in grams?
choices: 8 g
4 g
quiz.rationale: 8 x 500 mg = 4000 mg. Since 1000 mg = 1 g, the maximum is 4 g in 24 hours.
quiz.placement: Part B: safe and healthy environment (maximum paracetamol dose of 8 x 500 mg = 4 g in 24 hours)

quiz.prompt: Which responsibility of a learner helps keep a school laboratory safe and healthy?
choices: Tasting substances to find out what they are
Following lab rules such as wearing goggles and not tasting substances
Taking off goggles once the heating has started
Heating substances alone when the teacher is away
quiz.rationale: Safety rules such as wearing goggles, not tasting and heating only with supervision are the learner's responsibilities. They protect the learner and others in the laboratory.
quiz.placement: Part B: rights and responsibilities brainstorm and gallery presentation (linking to lab safety rules)

quiz.prompt: Why does an antacid tablet relieve heartburn while a paracetamol tablet relieves pain?
choices: Both tablets neutralise stomach acid, but paracetamol does it more slowly
The antacid acts on pain and fever, while paracetamol neutralises stomach acid
The antacid neutralises excess stomach acid, while paracetamol acts on pain and fever and does not neutralise acid
They act in the same way, but the antacid is a bigger tablet
quiz.rationale: The antacid (calcium carbonate) reacts with excess stomach acid, which is why it fizzes in acid such as vinegar. Paracetamol has a different action on pain and fever and does not fizz in acid.
quiz.placement: Step 2: explain the medicine puzzle (Wanjiru's question about the antacid and paracetamol)

quiz.prompt: Salt, sand, sulphur and iron filings all look like powders, but they behave very differently in water, in heat and near a magnet. What is the best explanation?
choices: Each substance has its own properties because of what it is made of
They behave differently only because their colours are different
They behave differently because they were bought from different shops
They behave differently only because the grains are different sizes
quiz.rationale: Properties such as solubility, magnetism and melting behaviour come from what each substance is made of. This is the claim and reasoning in the Final Explanation, and it is why chemists can choose or separate materials by their properties.
quiz.placement: Step 1: Claim-Evidence-Reasoning (CER) chart on why A-H behave differently

quiz.prompt: A friend says: "I took six paracetamol tablets (500 mg each) at once because my head hurts a lot." What is the best advice?
choices: Follow the label dose of 1 to 2 tablets every 4 to 6 hours with a maximum of 8 tablets in 24 hours, because too much can harm the liver
It is fine because paracetamol is sold in shops, so it is safe in any amount
Children and adults can take the same dose, so there is nothing to worry about
Take even more tablets, because a larger dose works faster
quiz.rationale: The label gives the correct dose. Taking too much paracetamol (over 4 g in 24 hours) can damage the liver, and being sold in a shop does not make a medicine safe in any amount.
quiz.placement: Step 2-3: probe on a friend taking six paracetamol tablets at once (using the label and dosage)

quiz.prompt: Which statement correctly classifies the substances from the Kisumu tray?
choices: Sulphur and iron are elements, while table salt and water are compounds
Sulphur and iron are compounds, while table salt and water are elements
Salt is an element because it dissolves in water
Mixture M of iron, sand and salt is a compound because it was separated
quiz.rationale: Sulphur and iron are elements. Table salt, water and sugar are compounds. Mixture M (iron, sand and salt) is a mixture whose parts can be separated by their properties.
quiz.placement: Step 2: redraw the final model, part (a) what the substances are made of
